# MCP reference

<!-- Generated by `UPDATE_MCP_DOCS=1 cargo test -p emulabzip-cli --test mcp_reference`. Do not edit by hand. -->

130 tools, 8 prompts and 13 resources, as `emulabzip mcp --allow-writes` offers them. Without `--allow-writes` the tools marked **Asks first** are not offered. See [MCP server](mcp.md) for how to connect and what is safe.

- **Reads** only looks.
- **Changes** acts on a device or on EmuLabZip's own files, and can be put back.
- **Asks first** destroys or rewrites data: only with `--allow-writes`, and each call asks the person to confirm.

Every tool that acts on a device also takes an optional `device` (an id or a name). An argument followed by `?` is optional.

## Screen, logs and reports

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `create_bug_report` | Write a bug report as one self-contained HTML file in EmuLabZip's reports folder: a screenshot, the device, the warnings and errors of the log, the failed requests and the readable crashes, from the device as it is now or from a recorded session. | `app`?, `description`?, `issue`?, `session`?, `title`?, `without`? | Changes |
| `read_logs` | Read recent log lines (logcat on Android, the unified log on iOS), filtered by app, level, tag or text. | `app`?, `grep`?, `level`?, `lines`?, `tag`? | Reads |
| `screenshot` | Take a screenshot of a device. |  | Reads |

## Devices and state

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `boot_device` | Start an emulator or simulator that is not running, and wait until it is up. | `device`, `headless`?, `platform`? | Changes |
| `compare_devices` | What differs between two devices: build, hardware, display, locale and the rest of the facts device_info reports, side by side. | `a`, `all`?, `b` | Reads |
| `create_device` | Make a new emulator or simulator from an image and a model that `device_options` lists. | `image`, `model`, `name`, `platform` | Changes |
| `delete_device` | Delete an emulator or simulator for good, with its apps and data. | `device`, `platform`? | Asks first |
| `delete_emulator_snapshot` | Delete an emulator snapshot. | `name` | Asks first |
| `device_info` | Facts about a device: build, hardware, display, battery, memory and locale. |  | Reads |
| `device_options` | What a new emulator or simulator can be made from: the system images or runtimes, and the device models, by id, with whether the image is installed. | `platform` | Reads |
| `diff_state` | What changed in the structure of an app's data between two saved states, or between a saved state and the app now: tables, columns, indexes and preference keys added, removed or changed. | `after`?, `before` | Reads |
| `list_all_devices` | List every emulator and simulator, running or not (a stopped one has state "shutdown"), with ids to start them with boot_device. | none | Reads |
| `list_apps` | List the apps on a device, with their package names or bundle ids, versions and process ids when running. | `all`?, `running`? | Reads |
| `list_devices` | List the running Android emulators, iOS simulators and attached devices, with their ids, state and OS version. | none | Reads |
| `list_emulator_snapshots` | The snapshots of a running Android emulator (its whole state, saved by the emulator itself). |  | Reads |
| `list_states` | The state files EmuLabZip has saved, newest first, by the names diff_state takes. | none | Reads |
| `load_emulator_snapshot` | Load an emulator snapshot: the emulator goes back to it, and the state it is in now is thrown away. | `name` | Asks first |
| `restore_state` | Put a saved state (from save_state) back into its app: the app's data is replaced. | `state` | Asks first |
| `save_emulator_snapshot` | Save the running Android emulator's whole state as a snapshot with this name. | `name` | Changes |
| `save_state` | Save an app's data (databases, preferences, files; not caches) to a state file kept by EmuLabZip, to compare later with diff_state. | `app`, `name`? | Changes |
| `shutdown_device` | Stop a running emulator or simulator. | `device`, `platform`? | Changes |
| `wipe_device` | Erase a device: every app and all its data are deleted, and it starts fresh. | `device`, `platform`? | Asks first |

## Input, flows and links

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `flow_create` | Write a flow by hand: a list of steps, each an object with a `type` (launch; tap {x,y}; longPress {x,y,ms}; swipe {x1,y1,x2,y2,ms}; text {text}; key {key}; wait {ms}) that play_flow can run, and flow_export can turn into Maestro. | `app`?, `height`?, `name`, `steps`, `width`? | Changes |
| `flow_export` | A saved flow as a Maestro YAML flow (`maestro`) or as a shell script of emulabzip commands (`script`), returned as text. | `flow`, `format` | Reads |
| `flow_show` | The steps of a saved flow, with their labels, and the screen size it was recorded on. | `flow` | Reads |
| `forget_link` | Take a link out of the deep link history. | `url` | Asks first |
| `input_text` | Type text into the focused field of an Android device. | `text` | Changes |
| `launch_app` | Start an app on the device, by package name or bundle id, as the launcher would. | `app` | Changes |
| `link_history` | The deep links opened and checked before, newest first, with the result of the last check and whether it is pinned. | none | Reads |
| `list_flows` | The saved flows: runs of touches, text and key presses recorded from a device (emulabzip flow record, or the Automation view), by id with their app and number of steps. | none | Reads |
| `open_url` | Open a web address or an app's own link on the device. | `url` | Changes |
| `play_flow` | Play a saved flow on an Android device: the taps, swipes, text and key presses that were recorded, scaled to this screen. | `flow` | Changes |
| `press_key` | Press a key on an Android device: back, home, enter, tab, delete, volume_up, app_switch… | `key` | Changes |
| `remove_flow` | Delete a saved flow. | `flow` | Asks first |
| `swipe` | Drag a finger across the screen of an Android device, from one point to another in pixels. | `duration_ms`?, `x1`, `x2`, `y1`, `y2` | Changes |
| `tap` | Touch a point of the screen of an Android device. | `x`, `y` | Changes |
| `verify_app_links` | Ask Android to verify an app's domains again (`pm verify-app-links --re-verify`), then run check_link after a few seconds to see whether it worked. | `app` | Changes |

## Device controls

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `control_appearance` | Switch the device between light and dark mode. | `mode` | Changes |
| `control_battery` | Pretend the battery is at a level, charging or not (Android); or go back to the real battery. | `charging`?, `level`?, `reset`? | Changes |
| `control_display_size` | Change the screen size (pixels) and density (dpi) of an Android device, or put them back with reset. | `density`?, `height`?, `reset`?, `width`? | Changes |
| `control_font_scale` | Make the device's text bigger or smaller, as a percentage of normal (100 is normal, 130 and 200 are common accessibility settings), to find text that does not fit. | `percent` | Changes |
| `control_info` | What a device supports changing, its appearance, and the permissions of an app when `app` is given. | `app` | Reads |
| `control_locale` | Show an app in another language or a pseudo-locale (en-XA for long text, ar-XB for right to left), to find text that does not fit; or put the language back. | `app`?, `locale`? | Changes |
| `control_location` | Change the device's location (emulators and simulators). | `lat`?, `lon`? | Changes |
| `control_notification` | Post a notification (Android) or send a simulated push to an app (iOS). | `app`?, `body`, `payload`?, `title` | Changes |
| `control_permission` | Grant, revoke or reset one permission of an app (an Android permission name, or an iOS service such as photos). | `action`, `app`, `permission` | Changes |
| `control_status_bar` | Show a clean status bar (fixed time, battery and signal), for screenshots; or clear the override. | `battery`?, `cellular`?, `clear`?, `time`?, `wifi`? | Changes |
| `list_plugins` | List the plugins installed on this computer: programs that collect their own data from a device. | none | Reads |
| `run_plugin` | Run an enabled plugin on a device and return what it reported: metrics, tables, text and log lines. | `app`?, `name`, `seconds`? | Changes |

## Performance

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `analyze_heap` | Take a heap dump of a debuggable Android app and look for leaks: destroyed Activities and removed Fragments still alive, each with the path from a GC root that keeps it, plus the objects that keep the most memory alive. | `all_heaps`?, `app` | Changes |
| `list_traces` | List the traces recorded with EmuLabZip (Perfetto system traces, simpleperf CPU profiles, Instruments recordings). | none | Reads |
| `measure_energy` | Measure the energy an app uses over a few seconds (at most 120). | `app`, `seconds`? | Changes |
| `measure_startup` | Time how long an app takes to open (cold, warm or hot), several times. | `app`, `kind`?, `runs`? | Changes |
| `memory_diff` | Where an app's memory grew: reads its memory, waits (while you use the app), reads again, and returns the categories that changed, largest first. | `app`, `seconds`? | Reads |
| `memory_report` | Where an app's memory goes: PSS by category on Android, footprint by VM region on iOS. | `app` | Reads |
| `perf_snapshot` | Measure CPU, memory, frame rate and battery for a few seconds: samples one second apart, device-wide or for one app. | `app`?, `samples`? | Reads |
| `record_trace` | Record a trace on a device and keep it in the library: a Perfetto system trace (Android), a simpleperf CPU profile (Android) or an Instruments template (iOS Simulator). | `app`?, `duration_s`?, `kind`, `preset`?, `system_wide`?, `template`? | Changes |
| `trace_query` | Run PerfettoSQL on a Perfetto recording (tables such as slice, sched, thread, process, counter). | `id`, `sql` | Reads |
| `trace_summary` | Summarize a recording: for a Perfetto trace, CPU by process and thread, frame times and jank, memory and the busiest slices; for a CPU profile, the hottest functions. | `id` | Reads |

## Quality

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `analyze_package` | Break an APK, AAB or IPA file down by kind (dex, native, resources, assets), folder, ABI and dex file, with its biggest files and method count. | `file`, `top`? | Reads |
| `audit_accessibility` | Check the screen in front for accessibility problems: tappable views without a name, touch targets under 48 dp (Android) or 44 pt (iOS), text with too little contrast, and neighbours that sound the same. |  | Reads |
| `audit_security` | Audit an installed app for security and privacy problems that are not about speed: secrets and personal data in the log, preferences and databases; the debuggable and allowBackup flags; components other apps can reach; App Transport Security exceptions and missing privacy manifest domains on iOS. | `app`, `only`? | Reads |
| `check_link` | Check a deep link: whether the domain's assetlinks.json (Android) or apple-app-site-association (iOS) lists the app, whether the app's signing key or team id matches, what the device decided about the domain, and which app opens the link. | `app`?, `url` | Reads |
| `check_text` | Check the screen for text that does not fit: cut off, pushed past the edge of the screen, clipped by its container, or (with rtl) not mirrored for a right-to-left language. | `rtl`? | Reads |
| `diff_packages` | What changed in size between two builds (APK, AAB or IPA): the total, each kind and folder, and the biggest files added, removed or changed. | `after`, `before`, `top`? | Reads |
| `get_layout` | The views on a device's screen as a tree: class, text, label, id, size and position, and whether each can be tapped. | `depth`? | Reads |
| `i18n_sweep` | Try the screen in other languages and text sizes and say what gets worse: text that is cut off, off screen, or not mirrored in a right-to-left language, and touch targets that shrink. | `app`?, `locales`?, `text_sizes`? | Changes |
| `package_budget` | Check an APK, AAB or IPA (full path on this computer) against size limits: total, dex, native code and resources in megabytes (compressed), method count, and growth in percent over a baseline build. | `baseline`?, `dex_mb`?, `file`, `growth_percent`?, `methods`?, `native_mb`?, `resources_mb`?, `total_mb`? | Reads |
| `simulate_color_blindness` | Show the screen as someone with colour blindness sees it (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia or achromatopsia): returns the findings of text that was readable normally and is not any more, and the changed screenshot. | `vision` | Reads |
| `visual_capture` | Keep the screen as a baseline for visual_compare: it is saved as a PNG in the project's `visual` folder. | `name` | Changes |
| `visual_compare` | Compare the screen with a baseline made by `emulabzip visual capture`: returns how much changed and where, and a picture with the changes in red. | `baseline` | Reads |
| `visual_list` | The visual baselines saved in the project's `visual` folder, with their sizes. | none | Reads |
| `visual_update` | Replace a visual baseline with the screen as it is now. | `name` | Asks first |

## Crashes

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `add_mapping` | Store a mapping.txt, a source map or a .dSYM (by its full path on this computer) for an app and build version, so crashes of that build read clearly from now on. | `app`, `file`, `version` | Changes |
| `get_crash` | One crash with its exception or signal, the stack of the thread that crashed (and others), and hints. | `id`, `original`?, `raw`? | Reads |
| `list_crashes` | List the crashes, native crashes and ANRs a device has recorded, newest first. | `app`?, `kind`? | Reads |
| `list_mappings` | The mappings, source maps and dSYMs EmuLabZip has stored to read crashes with, by app and build version. | `app`? | Reads |
| `remove_mapping` | Delete the mapping, source map or dSYM stored for an app version. | `app`, `version` | Asks first |
| `symbolicate_stack` | Make a pasted stack readable: Java frames are read with the app's `mapping.txt` (R8), JavaScript frames with its source map, for exactly the version given. | `app`, `stack`, `version` | Reads |

## Network

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `analytics_events` | The analytics events (Segment, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Firebase) found in the captured requests, decoded: the event's name, kind, properties and user. | `limit`?, `services`? | Reads |
| `net_breakpoints` | The requests and responses held at a breakpoint right now (a rule with the action breakpoint), with their headers and bodies. | none | Reads |
| `net_clear` | Forget the captured requests. | none | Changes |
| `net_conditions` | Slow, lag or cut the network the proxy gives the device, from a preset (fast-3g, slow-3g, slow-wifi, high-latency, packet-loss, offline) or with numbers, or `off` for the normal network. | `down_kbps`?, `latency_ms`?, `loss_percent`?, `off`?, `preset`?, `up_kbps`? | Changes |
| `net_connect_device` | Point a device at the proxy (an Android device's global proxy setting through adb, or the iOS Simulator's Mac proxy), starting the proxy first if needed. |  | Changes |
| `net_disconnect_device` | Put a device's network settings back to normal. |  | Changes |
| `net_export_har` | Save the captured requests as a HAR file in EmuLabZip's exports folder, named `<name>.har`. | `name` | Changes |
| `net_flow` | One captured request in full: headers, timing, the error, which rule changed it, an OpenAPI contract result, and the request and response bodies decoded (JSON pretty-printed, images returned as images). | `bodies`?, `id`, `max_chars`? | Reads |
| `net_flows` | The requests the proxy saw, as short rows: id, method, address, status, size, time, and why one failed, which rule touched it and any contract violations. | `host`?, `limit`?, `method`?, `path`?, `since_id`?, `status`?, `text`? | Reads |
| `net_install_ca` | Make a device trust the proxy's certificate, so HTTPS can be read: the system store on an emulator without Google Play, the simulator's keychain on iOS. |  | Changes |
| `net_replay` | Answer the app's requests from a recording, so it runs offline and the same every time: a recorded session (list_sessions) or a HAR file from net_export_har. | `har`?, `passthrough`?, `session`? | Changes |
| `net_replay_stop` | Go back to asking the real servers. | none | Changes |
| `net_resend` | Send a captured request again, with changes if asked (method, address, headers, body). | `body_text`?, `headers`?, `id`, `method`?, `url`? | Changes |
| `net_resume` | Let a held message go on, optionally with edited headers, body or status, or fail the request with abort. | `abort`?, `body_text`?, `headers`?, `id`, `status`? | Changes |
| `net_resume_all` | Release everything held at a breakpoint, unchanged. | none | Changes |
| `net_rules_get` | The rules in force: mocks, delays, blocks, breakpoints, map to a file or another server, OpenAPI checks and scripts. | none | Reads |
| `net_rules_set` | Replace the rules in force (send the whole list; net_rules_get shows the current one). | `rules` | Changes |
| `net_start` | Start the network proxy on this computer, so a device's HTTPS traffic can be read. | `http3`?, `port`? | Changes |
| `net_status` | Whether the proxy is running and on which port, the devices pointed at it, how many requests were seen, the rules, the network conditions and any recording being replayed. | none | Reads |
| `net_stop` | Stop the proxy and put every device this session pointed at it back to normal. | none | Changes |
| `openapi_check` | Check the captured responses against an OpenAPI 3 file (JSON or YAML, given by its full path on this computer): each response that does not match, with where in the body and why. | `host`?, `spec` | Reads |

## Live watches

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `watch_list` | The watches that exist: id, kind, device, how long, how many items are waiting, and whether it still runs. | none | Reads |
| `watch_read` | What a watch has gathered since `since` (everything kept without it), at most `limit` items, oldest first. | `id`, `limit`?, `since`? | Reads |
| `watch_start` | Follow something in the background and read it later with watch_read: `logs` (with level, tag and text filters), `perf` samples, `touches` on an Android screen, a WebView's `webview_console` or `webview_network` (its requests also appear in net_flows), a React Native app's `react_console` or `react_actions` (Redux). | `app`?, `grep`?, `interval_seconds`?, `kind`, `level`?, `metro_port`?, `page`?, `socket`?, `tag`? | Changes |
| `watch_stop` | Stop a watch and forget what it gathered. | `id` | Changes |

## Sessions

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `delete_session` | Delete a recorded session for good. | `id` | Asks first |
| `list_sessions` | List the sessions recorded with EmuLabZip (`emulabzip session record`, `emulabzip ci`, or the app), newest first. | none | Reads |
| `session_compare` | Compare two recorded sessions: the numbers (start time, frame rate, memory, errors, slow requests…) that got worse by more than a tolerance. | `baseline`, `run`, `tolerance_percent`? | Reads |
| `session_start` | Start recording a session: the log, performance samples, crashes, and optionally the screen (video_seconds), touches, screenshots and the network, all on one time axis. | `app`?, `name`?, `network`?, `screenshot_every_seconds`?, `touches`?, `video_seconds`? | Changes |
| `session_status` | How the session that is recording is going: how long, how many log lines, samples, crashes, touches and video pieces so far. | none | Reads |
| `session_stop` | Stop the session that is recording and save it. | none | Changes |
| `session_summary` | Summarize a recorded session: duration, log errors and the most repeated ones, crashes, requests and the slowest, CPU and memory peaks. | `id` | Reads |
| `session_timeline` | Everything a recorded session captured on one time axis, oldest first: touches, log warnings and errors, requests, slow frames (a stutter is one event), garbage collections, crashes, screenshots and pieces of screen video. | `id`, `lanes`?, `limit`? | Reads |

| Tool | Does | Arguments | |
|------|------|-----------|--|
| `list_files` | List an app's storage roots, or a folder in one. | `app`, `path`?, `root`? | Reads |
| `read_database` | Read a database in an app's sandbox without changing it: SQLite (with its write-ahead log, so recent writes show), a Realm file, or a Core Data store. | `app`, `limit`?, `offset`?, `path`, `root`, `sql`?, `table`? | Reads |

| `storage_roots` | The places an app keeps files that can be read: `data`, `external`, `cache` on Android (a debuggable app), the data, bundle and app group containers on iOS. | `app` | Reads |
| `write_file` | Replace a file in an app's own storage with text. | `app`, `path`, `root`, `text` | Asks first |

| `react_state` | The state of a React Native development app: Redux stores, React Query caches, React contexts and stores registered in globalThis.__EMULABZIP_STORES__, read through Metro (must be running). | `app`, `metro_port`? | Reads |
| `react_tree` | The React component tree of a React Native development app, with props, read through Metro (must be running). | `app`, `metro_port`? | Reads |

| `webview_list` | The WebViews and browsers on an Android device that can be inspected (a WebView in a debuggable app that turned on WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled, or Chrome), each with its pages: id, title and address. |  | Reads |
| `webview_reload` | Reload a WebView page, ignoring its cache. | `app`?, `page`?, `socket`? | Changes |

## Prompts

Ready-made plans an assistant can start from. Each names the tools to call.

| Prompt | For | Arguments |
|--------|-----|-----------|
| `explain_crash` | Find the latest crash, read it with the app's mapping, and say what went wrong and how to fix it. | `app`?, `crash_id`? |
| `why_is_it_slow` | Measure CPU, memory, frames and startup, then trace the slow part and say what to change. | `app`, `screen`? |
| `summarize_session` | Read a recorded session and say what happened: errors, crashes, slow requests and the moment it went wrong. | `session_id`? |
| `reproduce_bug` | Follow a description on the device, record what happens, and produce a bug report. | `description`, `app` |
| `debug_request` | Capture the app's traffic, find the request, and say why it failed or what it sent. | `url_or_host`? |
| `release_check` | Run the security, accessibility, size, text and language checks and list what to fix. | `app`, `package`? |
| `check_deep_link` | Test that a link opens the right screen of the app and that its domain is verified. | `url`, `app`? |
| `mock_backend` | Answer a host's requests with fixed responses, delays or errors, to test how the app copes. | `host`, `what`? |
